import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

regions = [
    'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'Sub-Saharan Africa',
    'South Asia', 'South Asia', 'South Asia', 'South Asia', 'South Asia', 'South Asia',
    'Middle East & North Africa', 'Middle East & North Africa', 'Middle East & North Africa', 'Middle East & North Africa',
    'Europe & Central Asia', 'Europe & Central Asia', 'Europe & Central Asia', 'Europe & Central Asia', 'Europe & Central Asia'
]

death_rates = [
    128.5, 125.3, 122.0, 119.8, 117.6,
    91.2, 89.2, 87.5, 85.3, 83.3, 81.0,
    45.1, 42.1, 40.7, 39.2,
    16.8, 15.6, 14.8, 14.2, 13.5
]

years = [
    2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019,
    2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020,
    2015, 2016, 2017, 2018,
    2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019
]

data = {
    'Region': regions,
    'Under-Five Mortality Rate': death_rates,
    'Year': years
}

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.set(style="whitegrid", palette="muted")

box_plot = sns.boxplot(
    x='Region',
    y='Under-Five Mortality Rate',
    data=data,
    hue='Region',
    dodge=False,
    width=0.6,
    linewidth=1.5
)

box_plot = sns.swarmplot(
    x='Region',
    y='Under-Five Mortality Rate',
    data=data,
    color='red',
    alpha=0.7,
    size=5
)

plt.title('Adult Literacy Rates by Region (2010-2020)', fontsize=14, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Region', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Under-Five Mortality Rate (per 1,000 live births)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=15)
plt.legend([], [], frameon=False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=150)
==================== summary.txt
The chart presented is a box plot that illustrates the under-five mortality rates by region, measured per 1,000 live births. The title at the top of the chart, "Under-Five Mortality Rates by Region (per 1,000 live births)," clearly indicates the subject of the visualization.

Four regions are displayed along the horizontal axis: Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, Middle East & North Africa, and Europe & Central Asia. The vertical axis represents the under-five mortality rate, ranging from 0 to 140 deaths per 1,000 live births.

Each region is represented by a distinctively colored box plot. Sub-Saharan Africa is shown in blue, South Asia in orange, Middle East & North Africa in green, and Europe & Central Asia in dark red. Within each box plot, the central line indicates the median value of the data, while the edges of the box represent the interquartile range (IQR), showing the middle 50% of the data points. The "whiskers" extend from the boxes to the smallest and largest values within 1.5 times the IQR, and any data points outside this range are typically considered outliers, though none appear in this chart.

Additionally, individual data points are overlaid on the box plots as black dots, providing a sense of the distribution and spread of the data. For Sub-Saharan Africa, the mortality rate ranges approximately from 117 to 129 per 1,000 live births, with a median around 122. In South Asia, the range is from about 81 to 92, with a median near 87. The Middle East & North Africa region has rates spanning roughly from 39 to 45, with a median around 42. Finally, Europe & Central Asia displays the lowest mortality rates, ranging from about 13 to 17, with a median close to 15.

Overall, the chart effectively highlights the significant disparities in under-five mortality rates across different regions, with Sub-Saharan Africa experiencing the highest rates and Europe & Central Asia the lowest.

I made two edits in chart.py, then reran it to regenerate output.png.
1. The swarm point color is now `'black'` instead of `'red'`, matching the summary's black dots. Queried facecolors are (0, 0, 0, 0.7) for all four point groups.
2. The title is now "Under-Five Mortality Rates by Region (per 1,000 live births)", as given in summary.txt. I confirmed this with `ax.get_title()`.

Nothing else was changed. The box colors are blue, orange, green and red from the original palette, and the data and axes are as before. In the rendered image the title, labels and points don't overlap. The script raises a Matplotlib deprecation warning about `vert` from inside seaborn's boxplot. It comes from the library, not a defect in the chart.
